value.rationale: The joint asymptotic law for random distances near diameter in a disk-clipped square has genuine geometric motivation: a rounding-to-polygon degeneration changes the tail exponent and admits two distinct boundary layers. The exact universal functions H and J are not mechanical restatements of disk/square marginals and can be used to analyze rare long-distance pairs and shape-induced tail phase changes. The fixed disk and square coefficients alone are established phenomena and are not the proposed novelty.
